clue.text: Contrarian to go astray, drinking Calvados, wanting a cocktail

indicators.note: to drink is to take something in, so the verb phrase swallows the other letters

parts.note: to go astray is to deviate from the right path

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the single letter a must be removed from the brandy's name
a cocktail is a mixture, signalling that the remaining letters of the brandy are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drinker strays from the path, knocking back apple brandy because no cocktail is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' tempts as a drink in the surface, but with 'wanting' it works on the brandy name: lose one A, mix the remaining seven letters, and 'drinking' sets them inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues the opposing side for argument's sake is a contrarian, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Nonsense about Church backing learner to perform tricky manoeuvre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nonsense phrase wraps the other letters

parts.note: double Dutch is gibberish, talk nobody can understand

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the church abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: CE is short for Church of England
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A driving test pupil attempts something complicated while someone mutters nonsense about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Double Dutch is British slang for gibberish; 'backing' turns the Church of England letters round, and with the learner they split the phrase after its seventh letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-declutching is a gear-changing technique, pressing the clutch twice, once thought tricky to master.

clue.text: Plant girl round peak

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the girl's name goes around the mountain word

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A young woman stands beside a mountain summit with a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a flowering garden plant, also called vervain, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: City man stashing diamonds

indicators.note: stashing means hiding away inside, so the man's name holds the jewels

parts.note: Lester is a man's name
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A city man has hidden a cache of diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is an English city in the East Midlands, an example of a city.

clue.text: Cast laid off in the compound

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors have been made redundant inside the walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a walled area for the laid-off actors; it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid salt is a chemical compound in which some hydrogen of an acid remains unreplaced.

clue.text: Love — including love of vessels

indicators.note: including means containing, so the goddess's name holds the other letter

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A person speaks of love in which there is love for ships.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'love's do different jobs: the goddess VENUS and the tennis zero O.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous means relating to veins, which are blood vessels, so it is an adjective meaning of vessels.

clue.text: Half-whimsical island

indicators.note: half signals taking only the first half of the synonym's letters

parts.note: capricious means whimsical, given to sudden changes of mood

explanation.surface: An island that is somewhat fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first five of the ten letters of CAPRICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples, an example of an island.

clue.text: Make mincemeat of counteroffensive

indicators.note: offensive in its sense of attacking suggests the preceding letters are assaulted and reordered

explanation.surface: A military counterattack makes mincemeat of the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counteroffensive' looks like one word, but splits into the fodder COUNTER and the anagram signal 'offensive'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to defeat heavily, the same as to make mincemeat of an opponent, an idiom.

clue.text: Stadium-bound in decline?

definitions.meaning: heading for the greyhound stadium, where people watch dogs race

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the dogs' means greyhound racing, held at a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deteriorating badly, while read literally it is a trip to a greyhound track.

clue.text: Nation and its typical weather shown to boy from another

parts.note: UK is short for the United Kingdom, a nation
rain is famously the UK's typical weather
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A country and its usual drizzle are shown to a lad from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from another' completes the sense 'from another nation': a person or thing from Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukrainian describes something from Ukraine, another nation than the one named first in the clue.

clue.text: Advertisement for doctor

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An advertisement placed on behalf of a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional piece, an informal word for an advertisement.

clue.text: Say something insincere about European city

parts.note: a lie is something insincere, an untruth

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the abbreviation for say is reversed

parts.note: eg, short for exempli gratia, means say or for example

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lie about a city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a verb going with 'something insincere', but it is the abbreviation for 'for example', which 'about' turns round after the untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium, an example of a European city.

clue.text: See 19
Help to reverse scarf's expansion

indicators.note: to reverse means to be read backwards, so the word for help is turned round

parts.note: aid means help
a stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: Helping to turn a scarf round so that it spreads out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle relaxes and its chambers expand and fill.

clue.text: Whip receives salutation — it's often found in small print

definitions.text: it's often found in small print

indicators.note: receives means takes inside, so the whip holds the greeting

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A whip is greeted, in what reads like a legal disclaimer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or proviso, typically tucked away in a contract's fine print.

clue.text: Claim memory is preserved by this philosophy?

parts.note: to aver is to claim or assert

indicators.note: being preserved by something means being kept inside it, so the word is goes inside the memory

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: Someone claims that this philosophy keeps memories intact.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' does double service only on the surface: it is the letters IS, with 'preserved by' putting them in ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Averroism is the medieval philosophical school following Averroes, the Arab commentator on Aristotle.

clue.text: Admirer finds time on the Continent for composition

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: A fan finds time while in Europe to listen to a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Continent' suggests mainland Europe to a British reader; here it is any continent, ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a free-form musical composition, an example of a composition.

clue.text: Eloquent character, one finishing cake amid company

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the abbreviation for company wraps the other piece

parts.note: an icer is someone who ices a cake, the final step

explanation.surface: A fluent speaker puts the finishing touch on a cake among friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing cake' looks like a last-letter pick (E); it is ICER, one who ices.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the Roman orator famous for his eloquence, an example of an eloquent character.

clue.text: Blood-feuder's pill contains uranium

definitions.note: the clue word is possessive with 's standing for is, which links to the wordplay

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the pill wraps the element symbol

parts.note: a caplet is a smooth coated tablet
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A man in a vendetta takes a radioactive tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capulets feud bloodily with the Montagues in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capulet belongs to Juliet's family, locked in a deadly feud with the Montagues in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Drunken sot craving drop of Niersteiner, Beaune or the like?

indicators.note: drunken means unsteady and disordered, so the letters reel into a new order
a drop of something is a tiny bit, here the opening letter

explanation.surface: A drunk longs for a little German white or a French red.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is SOT CRAVING, the N from 'drop of Niersteiner', and BEAUNE; the two named wines are fodder, so 'or the like?' is the definition: another wine of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabernet Sauvignon is a wine, like the named Niersteiner and Beaune, hence one of the like.

clue.text: It's unjust for one river (Burns's) to rise above another

indicators.note: in a down entry above means placed before the following letter
in a down entry, to rise means to read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Robert Burns wrote the song Sweet Afton about the river Afton
another river, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: It is unfair that one of Burns's rivers flows uphill over another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns I and AFTON into NOTFAI; R sits beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Not fair is a plain phrase for unjust or unfair.

clue.text: Repeatedly voice disapproval of clanger

indicators.note: repeatedly signals the jeering word appears twice

parts.note: to boo is to voice disapproval of someone

explanation.surface: Someone jeers again and again at a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo-boo is an informal word for a silly mistake, a synonym of clanger.

clue.text: Pouts petulantly about new look on top — on top

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the hairstyle
petulantly suggests a sulky fidget, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a perm is a new hairstyle, a fresh look on top of the head

explanation.surface: Someone sulks over their new hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'petulantly' rearranges POUTS into UPOST, which goes 'about' PERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest, a synonym of on top.

clue.text: Strong drink secures explosive discharge

indicators.note: secures means holds fast within, so the drink wraps the explosive

parts.note: rum is a strong spirit
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A stiff drink has an explosive effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, a synonym of discharge.

clue.text: Leave service, relinquishing right to join up again

indicators.note: relinquishing means giving up, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to retire is to leave service or employment

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the army, giving up the right to re-enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up' suggests re-enlisting; here it means tie together again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie a knot or laces is to join them up again, a literal sense.

clue.text: Have youngster left in primitive accommodation

indicators.note: in signals the letter goes inside the dwelling

parts.note: a cave is a primitive dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone gives birth, abandoned in a basic shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To calve is to give birth to a calf, so to have a young one.

clue.text: Finding turnip top in sink before a party is torture

indicators.note: before signals the sink piece comes ahead of the rest
in signals the first letter goes inside the sink

parts.note: a basin is a sink

indicators.note: a top is the uppermost part, here the opening letter

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Finding a turnip top in the sink before a party is a torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The bastinado is beating the soles of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastinado is a form of torture, caning the soles of the feet.

clue.text: Double room a steep outlay: we're 8, said 17

indicators.note: outlay read as out and lay suggests the letters are laid out anew
double signals the room word is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A double room is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossreferences are 8-down and 17-across: the famous orator lamented that the times and customs were in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin exclamation means 'oh the times, oh the customs', lamenting that society is deteriorating.
